statement: Deterministic generated source MUST be received through its owning review branch with exact input/output identity and no silent rebase, unrelated source mutation or model-mediated byte reconstruction.
because: Leader, 2026-10-13: move repeated deterministic work into existing responsible software and keep useful operation independent of the current conversation or model.
consumer: generator/generate-ci.mjs --pr and its later --verify-commit build consumer

specification.output: a verified source commit and owning draft review, or explicit unchanged/stale/unavailable result
specification.publication: non-forced Git ref update followed by authoritative ref and review readback; exact commit identity provides restart reconciliation
specification.treeReceiving: Bind exact base and result root identities by reconstructing Git tree objects along every declared output path. Verify complete immediate ancestor entries, Git mode/type/name/object identity and canonical tree encoding. Preserve every untouched sibling subtree by its identical object identity; do not enumerate its leaves. Refuse truncated or malformed objects, missing ancestors, undeclared changes, path/prefix collisions and symlink or file-kind changes. Read back the result's changed-path ancestors and exact output identities. This is complete transformation verification, not permission to accept a partial inventory.
specification.runnerSelection: Before a workflow source proposal, receive the explicit no-billing selector through a complete online repository runner inventory, or explicitly qualify a retained self-hosted selector from an authenticated prior same-repository default-branch run and started job. Historical source H, current generation base S and proposed bytes are distinct immutable inputs. Prove H-to-S unchanged per-job selectors, reusable supplier identities, permission and credential declarations, then prove S-to-proposal retention. Reject ambiguous/dynamic/unbound selectors, unresolved admission expressions and hidden grant changes. Historical execution establishes neither current availability nor future execution entitlement. Never silently fall back from a denied or failed inventory call.
specification.boundedAddedJob: Only an exact direct read-only job fragment produced by an independently qualified existing owner may join the retained-selector source proposal. Bind its producer, generation source, review branch, proposal identity and complete output fragment; require the identical self-hosted selector, explicit contents:read, no environment/secrets/container/services/credential grant, and preserve explicit checkout persist-credentials:false. No new reusable supplier or arbitrary job class is admitted. A fragment descriptor proves byte association, not review or execution approval.
specification.activationDeclarations: Expose event, job-if and concurrency differences for historical-to-current and current-to-proposed separately in the source receiving result. Source publication can trigger existing CI; those exact changes require ordinary independent owner review and existing authorized source-trigger admission. Do not invent a blanket no-trigger or draft-only execution rule. Actual scheduling, trust, no-spend and activation receiving remain at execution.
specification.sharedProofProvider: The default receiver requires the genuine @red-cup-engineering/git-services-section source-tree-patch API at version 4.1.1 or newer, declared as a required peer. The existing authenticated source selection/materialization owner must supply it; a version constraint is not source availability, package enrollment, public-registry installation or activation evidence. Keep missing provider and unqualified CI explicit.

design: Strengthen the existing generator/open-pr.mjs operation and migrate its actual caller. Preserve the generated proposal in its source commit and review. Re-run the same producer for later full-tree and byte parity. Do not create a separate controller, receipt repository, credential or deployment path.
receiving: Git-backed tests exercise the actual producer and receiver, stale/concurrent publication, lost replies, restart idempotence, counterfeit receipt trees and later CLI parity. A production descriptor generator needs its own qualified artifact-to-writer binding; the read-only machine build and PR-metadata intake do not confer source-writing authority. Source qualification does not close runtime recovery.
